text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

- The proposed merger between Norway' largest insurer Storebrand and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse was blocked on Thursday when private investor Kjell Inge Roekke and conglomerate Orkla voted against the deal. Roekke and Orkla hold 10 percent each in Storebrand.

- The public health authority has decide that McDonald's can resume selling its McLaks salmon burger on the Norwegian market. McLaks was withdrawn from sale at the beginning of June after four people became ill and were hospitalised apparently after eating the burgers. Despite the lifting of the ban, McDonalds says it will not yet put McLaks back on the menu.
- Norway and the European Union will start discussions on a new Schengen deal after summer.
- Norwegians now pay 100 billion crowns more per year in taxes than five years ago. Income taxes have increased by 45 percent in the same period.

- State-owned oil company Statoil has swapped a batch of British and Norwegian assets with oil giants British Petroleum and Chevron Corp and exchanged interests in Norwegian exploration licences with Norsk Hydro, Elf Aquitaine and Total.

- Norsk Hydro's new Njord oil platform will be ready four months ahead of schedule and cost 25 percent less than previous installations. However, constructor Aker Stord is demanding an additional one billion crowns for its work, claiming it was much more expensive than estimated.
